newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's AMP says no comment on Norwich report.
newsitem.headline: Australia's AMP says no comment on Norwich report.

text.p: Life insurer Australian Mutual Provident Society (AMP) said on Tuesday that it was looking to make international acquisitions but would not comment on reports that British insurance group Norwich Union was among its targets.
"It is part of our strategy to expand overseas," AMP communications manager Bob Pritchard told Reuters.
Britain's Times newspaper reported last Saturday that AMP was planning a takeover bid for Norwich after the British insurance group floats on the stock market next month.
The newspaper said AMP was working with merchant bank Morgan Stanley and planned to make a bid shortly after Norwich Union's float on June 16.
"We have indicated we are considering acquisitions in other markets but we have no intention of confirming or denying ... media speculation," Pritchard said.
"It wouldn't be a very smart strategy if we telegraphed our punches," he said.
AMP recently lost a battle to win control of mutually-owned insurance group Scottish Amicable when its offer was trumped by Britain's Prudential Corp Plc.
After its bid for Scottish Amicable, AMP said it was interested in a number of other acquisition opportunities in Britain.
